newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek stocks continue correction, give up 1.85pct.
newsitem.headline: Greek stocks continue correction, give up 1.85pct.

text.p: The Athens bourse ended 1.85 percent lower on Wednesday on moderate volume with brokers saying it was a healthy correction after gains of about 20 percent from the beginning of 1997.
"It may continue in the next one to three sessions, but this is a healthy market reaction to a 20 percent market rise from the beginning of 1997," said broker George Kotzambasis at Alki Securities.
He expected the market rise to continue after corrections with rallies in banks, cement shares and stocks of metallurgical companies.
"The market will regain its momentum, because of news of share capital increases by banks and the state's intention to part float public utilities and OTE telecom," he added.
The index could reach 1,200 points in the next three or four months especially if Athens is picked as a candidate for the 2,004 Olympics on March 5, he said.
Other brokers said they had been expecting the profit taking after Tuesday's high volume and last week's steep rise.

"We were expecting a correction at any moment, but the signal was given with Tuesday's high volume of 21.1 billion drachmas as investors have started to take profits," said John Sofronis, a broker at Voilis Securities.
The Athens general share index closed 1.85 percent or 20.51 points down at 1088.50 from Tuesday's 1109.01, after opening at 1106.97.

All sectoral indices were down with banks losing 1.77 percent, construction dropping 3.44 percent and investment shares ending 2.16 percent down. Small caps ended 1.71 percent down with industrials losing 1.65 percent.
Wednesday's turnover was moderate at 11.1 billion drachmas on volume of 4.1 million shares. Losers led gainers 173 to 40 with 25 issues unchanged on 238 traded.
